scenario: AITA for causing a friend to drop out of school? | I know my title sounds bad. I (17F) am currently in my senior year of school. Friend1 (18F) recently lost her dad to an accidental overdose. Her dad died the morning of a party our whole friend group was meant to attend. Friend2(17F) had no alcohol for this party (I know we're underage but in our country it's 18 not 21). Upon hearing about Friend1's dad on our groupchat, she said nothing. Fine. Whatever. That's none of my business. A shit thing to do considering they're close but not my place, I was more preoccupied with trying to make sure Friend1 was ok so I didn't want to bring it up. Our friend then messaged on this chat asking Friend1 if she was still going to the party and if not could she give her any alcohol she had bought for it. I thought this was absolutely out of order and I messaged her privately and send quite strong messages. I said it was a really cunty thing to do ON the day her dad died. I called her pathetic and said she should be ashamed of herself. This happened last weekend. She left our groupchat. Went to the party and then came to school on Monday and dropped out. She had said repeatedly before that she was only in school this year to hang out with us. Friend1 is obviously currently preoccupied with famy stuff and not petty friend drama but she did tell Friend2 to fuck off as well. I spoke to her briefly about it before I messaged privately. I'm now being blamed by friends of Friend2 who were not in the groupchat for her leaving school. They are saying I helped bully her out of school. AITA? I'm beginning to think I was because of how strongly worded my message was.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm AITA (Did I Act Too Aggressively) in this situation. Let me start by understanding the scenario fully. So, there's me, a 17-year-old girl, in my senior year of school. My friend, Friend1, who is 18, recently lost her dad to an accidental overdose. That's really tragic and I can imagine she's going through a tough time. The incident happened on the morning of a party that our whole friend group was supposed to attend. Another friend, Friend2, who is also 17, didn't have any alcohol for the party. I know we're underage, but in our country, the legal drinking age is 18, not 21 like in some places. Upon hearing about Friend1's dad passing away in our group chat, Friend2 didn't say anything. I thought that was fine, maybe she was just processing it or didn't know what to say. I was more focused on making sure Friend1 was okay, so I didn't want to bring it up in the group chat. Then, Friend2 messaged in the group chat asking Friend1 if she was still going to the party and if not, could she give her any alcohol she had bought for it. I found this absolutely out of order. It felt insensitive and inconsiderate, especially on the day her dad died. So, I messaged Friend2 privately and sent some pretty strong messages. I called her out for being "cunty" (which I think is slang for being mean or manipulative), and told her she should be ashamed of herself. This happened last weekend. After that, Friend2 left our group chat, went to the party, and then came to school on Monday and dropped out. She had mentioned before that she was only in school this year to hang out with us. Friend1 is obviously dealing with family stuff and isn't into the petty drama, but she did tell Friend2 to "fuck off" as well. I talked to Friend1 briefly about it before I messaged Friend2 privately. Now, I'm being blamed by some of Friend2's friends who weren't in the group chat for her leaving school. They're saying I helped bully her out of school. I'm starting to think I was AITA because of how strongly worded my messages were. So, the question is: Did I act too aggressively? Should I have handled the situation differently? Is there a better way to address Friend2's insensitivity without causing such a strong reaction? First, I need to consider the context. Friend1 was going through a traumatic event, losing her dad. It's important to be supportive and understanding in such situations. Friend2's message asking for alcohol after hearing about the tragedy was indeed insensitive. It's natural to feel upset and want to confront her about it. However, the way I confronted her was through strong, direct messages. While it's important to stand up for a friend, using harsh language might have escalated the situation. It could have made Friend2 feel attacked rather than understood, leading to her leaving the group chat and eventually dropping out of school. I also need to think about the impact of my actions on the group dynamic. By addressing Friend2 privately, I might have prevented public embarrassment, but the strength of my words could have been too much. It's possible that she felt unsupported or judged, contributing to her decision to leave school. Additionally, considering the role of other friends, it's clear that the situation has caused tension within the group. Friend2's friends are now blaming me, which adds another layer of complexity. It's important to reflect on how my actions might have been perceived by others and whether there's a way to mend the relationships. In summary, while I had good intentions to support Friend1 and address Friend2's insensitivity, the way I did it might have been too aggressive. It's possible that a more empathetic or diplomatic approach could have diffused the situation better and prevented Friend2 from feeling pushed away. I should also consider seeking advice from a trusted adult or counselor to navigate these complex social dynamics, especially given the emotional nature of the situation. It's important to balance standing up for friends with maintaining healthy relationships and considering the feelings of everyone involved.
